transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Iraq is celebrating Sovereignty Day, more than 20 years after the U.S. invasion, the
last American troops have withdrawn.
Retired Lieutenant General H.R. McMaster was President Trump's national security advisor
during his first term.
McMaster also served in Iraq during both Gulf wars.
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition about whether the mission should have ended now while the
U.S. is at war with Iran.
This is going to embolden, I think, the Iranians to a certain extent, and it's not clear that
there has been the enduring defeat of ISIS.
Remember, that became the most destructive terrorist organization in history, taking control
of territory the size of Great Britain, and conducting something like 95 attacks outside
of the area that it controlled, including, of course, remember in Brussels, in Paris,
and Marseille, and so forth.
So I think it's really important to ensure the enduring defeat of ISIS, and having troops
there helps you.
It just helps you develop the intelligence picture and work with Iraqis who are doing
the majority of the fighting.
McMaster is a senior fellow at the Hoover Institution.
Meanwhile, President Trump is celebrating the withdrawal on social media today.
He credited himself for that.
A former Cornell University student's lawsuit alleging she was sexually assaulted by seven
male students at a fraternity party is renewing questions about how colleges deal with reports
of violent crime.
Here's NPR's Alyssa Networney.
Title IX prohibits discrimination in schools based on sex.
Under that law, the school's job is to make sure all students have a safe campus environment,
equal access to an education.
In the case of Cornell University, when the district attorney did not move forward with
the criminal investigation back in 2024, the campus Title IX process got underway.
In a statement, Cornell said its investigation took several months and led to expulsions
and suspensions.
The fraternity chapter was closed in 2024.
Title IX has a lower burden of proof than a criminal case.
But in recent years, there have been big changes.
The Trump administration raised the burden of proof and also now requires schools to
conduct "live hearings" with cross-examination.
Alyssa Networney, NPR News.
New York City Mayor Zara Mamdani has released a report on anti-Semitism and a strategy to
combat the prejudice.
More from NPR's Jason DeRose.
In a video released by the mayor's office, Mamdani says he spent this year listening
to Jewish New Yorkers.
What he's learned...
Anti-Semitism is real and it is growing.
The report says that although Jews make up just 12% of the city's population, anti-Jewish
hate crimes account for more than half of all confirmed hate crimes in New York, something
the mayor calls unacceptable.
Jewish New Yorkers should feel cherished and celebrated in the most Jewish city in America.
The report, however, does not define anti-Semitism, and critics say Mamdani's repeated labeling
of the war in Gaza as genocide has led to increased anti-Jewish sentiment.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
This is NPR.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has added a second measles death to its national
tally this year.
It comes after Pennsylvania reported four deaths linked to measles, NPR's Maria Godoy has details.
The CDC website did not identify where the death occurred, so it's unclear if the new
death is one of the four reported in Pennsylvania.
No other state has reported a measles-associated death this year.
The deaths have become wrapped up in a political feud between Pennsylvania's Democratic Governor
Josh Shapiro and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
When Shapiro announced the first two deaths, Kennedy initially questioned whether they were
due to measles, and in a highly unusual move, the CDC initially excluded them from its weekly
measles tally.
The CDC says it's working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to
develop a standardized definition for deaths due to measles.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
The U.S. economy expanded at a pace of 2.2 percent in the second quarter.
The Commerce Department says consumer spending and business investment were strong.
Love, that sweater from Macy's.
Keep it, change your mind, maybe door-dash it back.
The service is known mainly for delivering your restaurant food or groceries, but DoorDash
says that as of November, it also plans to start offering nationwide services for picking
up or returning items you buy from participating retail stores through its app.
Macy's, Anthropology, and The North Face are among the latest companies to formally
sign on.
DoorDash's rival UberEats also in the retail delivery business have partnered with Costco
and Footlocker, it's NPR.

topics.text: Iraq celebrates Sovereignty Day more than 20 years after U.S. invasion, American troops withdrawn
Former Cornell University student sues over alleged sexual assault by seven male fraternity students
New York City Mayor Zara Mamdani releases report on anti-Semitism and strategy to combat it
CDC adds second measles death to national tally this year after Pennsylvania reports four deaths
U.S. economy expanded at 2.2 percent pace in second quarter, strong consumer and business spending
DoorDash plans nationwide retail return and pickup service starting November with major store partnerships
